The first time a write batch is committed for a given bucket, the newly-formed document is inserted.
On subsequent batch commits, we perform an update operation.

statements.statement: numBucketInserts counts new buckets and numBucketUpdates counts updates to existing buckets.
MongoDB's design README says the first committed write batch inserts a bucket and later batches update it.
statements.note: bucket_catalog README in mongodb/mongo says exactly this.

edits.rationale: The serverStatus manual defines numBucketInserts as new buckets created and numBucketUpdates as updates to an existing bucket. The MongoDB source tree's bucket_catalog README states the first committed write batch inserts the bucket document and later commits perform updates.

edits.old: MongoDB documents `serverStatus.bucketCatalog` as instance-level time-series metrics. `$collStats` exposes `storageStats.timeseries` only when the `storageStats` option is specified; the manual’s time-series example uses `storageStats: {}` for the default scale, and the option also permits `storageStats: { scale: <number> }`. For a sharded collection, `$collStats` returns one document per shard, so interpret the outputs at their own scopes. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

For a sharded collection, $collStats returns one document per shard. edits.old: MongoDB describes the `$collStats` time-series fields as internal diagnostic data; the collection-level document includes bucket counters that overlap with `serverStatus.bucketCatalog` but uses a different schema. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20)
edits.new: MongoDB describes the $collStats time-series output as time series data for internal diagnostic use, and points to bucketCatalog for the fields. The example collection-level document shares some counters with serverStatus.bucketCatalog (e.g. numBucketInserts, numBucketUpdates) but also has fields such as bucketsNs, bucketCount, avgBucketSize and numActiveBuckets that the serverStatus metric table does not list. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/collStats.md

evidence.quote: The query returns a result similar to the following, which includes time series data for internal diagnostic use:

bucketsNs: 'test.weather',
   bucketCount: 12,
   avgBucketSize: 300,
   numActiveBuckets: 1,
   numBucketInserts: 12,
   numBucketUpdates: 0,
| `numBuckets` | The total number of tracked buckets. Expected to be equal to the sum of `numOpenBuckets` and `numArchivedBuckets`. |

statements.statement: MongoDB describes the $collStats time-series fields as internal diagnostic data.
The collection-level document includes bucket counters that overlap with serverStatus.bucketCatalog but uses a different schema.
statements.note: Overlap and differing field sets are observable by comparing the pages; docs don't say 'different schema' explicitly.

edits.rationale: The collStats page labels the output internal diagnostic and refers to bucketCatalog. Comparing the two pages shows overlapping counters and different field sets, but MongoDB does not explicitly state 'different schema', so the claim is restated as an observed difference.
